```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse=TRUE, comment="#>", message=FALSE, warning=FALSE,
  fig.width=8, fig.height=4.5, dpi=144)
library(L0glm)
options(width=90, digits=3)
```

L0glm fits sparse generalized linear models using adaptive ridge and IRLS.
The same interface covers ordinary GLMs, negative binomial counts, joint
multinomial classification and Cox survival models. Coefficients are returned
on the original predictor scale in a sparse matrix.

## Install

```{r install, eval=FALSE}
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("tomwenseleers/L0glm", subdir="L0glm")
```

The source package lives in the repository's `L0glm/` directory.
Windows source installation requires [Rtools](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/).
Special families use `mgcv`; Cox responses use `survival`.

## Fit a sparse model

Here two predictors carry the signal among thirty candidates.

```{r fit}
set.seed(7)
X <- matrix(rnorm(400 * 30), 400, 30)
beta <- numeric(30)
beta[c(1, 8)] <- c(2, -1.5)
y <- as.numeric(X %*% beta) + rnorm(400)

fit <- L0glm.fit(X, y, family=gaussian(), lambda="gic", relaxed=TRUE)
fit
```

`lambda="gic"` sets a penalty of `log(p) * log(log(n))` on the
minus-twice-log-likelihood scale. `relaxed=TRUE` refits the selected support
with negligible ridge penalization, giving the selected effects little shrinkage.

```{r recovery}
L0glm.metrics(fit, beta_true=beta)[c("gic", "TP", "FP", "FN", "TN", "F1_score", "MCC")]
```

True coefficients are supplied only to calculate recovery metrics; fitting uses `X` and `y`.

## Predict and inspect

```{r predict}
predict(fit, X[1:5, , drop=FALSE])
head(as.matrix(coef(fit)), 10)
c(logLik=as.numeric(logLik(fit)), AIC=AIC(fit), BIC=BIC(fit), GIC=GIC(fit))
```

`summary(fit)` adds a compact coefficient display and convergence diagnostics.
`fitted(fit)` returns fitted means for the training observations.
For new data, `predict()` applies the model in the original predictor coordinates.

## Change the family

```{r binomial}
set.seed(8)
y_binary <- rbinom(400, 1, plogis(.3 + X[, 1] - X[, 8]))
binary <- L0glm.fit(X, y_binary, family=binomial(),
  lambda="gic", relaxed=TRUE, maxit=100)
predict(binary, X[1:5, ], type="response")
```

Standard family objects and links work as in `stats::glm()`. Add an intercept
with `intercept=TRUE`; binomial and multinomial fits include one by default.
See the [negative binomial](negative-binomial.html),
[multinomial](multinomial.html) and [Cox](cox.html) tutorials for their response formats.

## Choose a workflow

| Task | Main function |
|---|---|
| One fast preset fit | `L0glm.fit(..., lambda="gic")` |
| Tune a penalty using an information criterion | `L0glm.tune(..., tune="gic")` |
| Cross-validate prediction deviance | `L0glm.tune(..., tune="cv", nfolds=5)` |
| Compare sparse regression methods | `sparseglm()` |
| Score predictions and support recovery | `L0glm.metrics()` |
| Screen an ultrahigh-dimensional design | `L0glm.fit(..., screen="ISIS")` |

Continue with [model selection](selection.html),
[weights and validation stopping](controls.html), or the
[million-predictor example](high-dimensional.html).
